explanation:
[EFFECT] Humidity has a non-monotonic effect with a clear penalty at extremes: moderate humidity (roughly 20–60%) produces small positive contributions (~+0.05 to +0.15), but very high humidity (above ~75–80%) drives contributions sharply negative, reaching around −0.7 to −0.8 near 100% humidity. Very low humidity shows some negative scatter but those are sparse observations.
[IMPORTANCE] This is a moderate-importance feature with a vertical range of roughly 0.9 log-units, similar in magnitude to month.
[RECOMMENDATION] Plan your staffing and bike availability primarily around the hour of the day — the evening peak (around 5–6 pm) and the morning shoulder (around 8 am) drive the largest swings in demand — and use temperature as the key weather signal, targeting comfortable mild days (~20–25 °C) for maximum expected ridership and scaling back during cold or very hot spells.
